questions.q: What does the @freq_type parameter of sp_add_schedule control?
options: The overall recurrence pattern — once, daily, weekly, or monthly
Which operator gets notified
The job's step order
The subsystem the job step runs under
questions.explain: freq_type sets the schedule's overall pattern (1=once, 4=daily, 8=weekly, 16=monthly); other parameters like freq_interval are interpreted relative to it.

questions.q: For a weekly schedule (freq_type = 8), what does @freq_interval represent?
options: A bitmask of days of the week (e.g. 62 for Monday through Friday)
The number of weeks between runs, always
The hour of the day the job runs
The number of retries allowed
questions.explain: For weekly schedules, freq_interval is a bitmask where each day of the week has a bit value (1=Sunday, 2=Monday, 4=Tuesday, etc.), OR'd together.

questions.q: Two different jobs both need to run every weekday at 1 AM. What's the recommended approach?
options: Create one schedule with sp_add_schedule and attach it to both jobs with sp_attach_schedule
Create two separate, identical schedule objects, one per job
Schedules cannot be shared between jobs under any circumstances
Put the frequency logic directly into each job's steps instead of using a schedule
questions.explain: A schedule is a standalone object in sysschedules; the same schedule can be attached to multiple jobs via sp_attach_schedule, avoiding duplicated frequency definitions.

options: Repeating the job within the active time window, e.g. every 15 minutes
The total number of days the schedule stays active
Which day of the month the job runs
The owner login of the schedule
questions.explain: freq_subday_type (minutes/hours) with freq_subday_interval sets a repeating cadence within the active_start_time to active_end_time window.

questions.q: Which system stored procedure links an existing schedule to a specific job?
options: sp_attach_schedule
sp_add_schedule
sp_add_jobserver
sp_add_jobstep
questions.explain: sp_add_schedule only creates the schedule object; sp_attach_schedule creates the link in msdb.dbo.sysjobschedules between a job and that schedule.
